title: Vue Practices & Smells
body:
# Vue Practices & Code Smells

## Small, cohesive components

A component should explain itself in one screenful. When you need "and also…"
to describe it, split by responsibility (display vs fetching vs layout).
The lesson workspace here splits Outline/Editor/Output/Quiz for exactly this
reason.

## Smell: prop drilling

```text
App → Page → Panel → Row → Badge(label)   // 4 hops passing `label`
```

**Why** it hurts: every intermediate layer carries data it ignores; refactors
touch five files.
**Refactor:** shared Pinia store near consumers, or provide/inject for scoped
framework-ish values (theme, i18n). Two levels of drilling is fine; five is a
signal.

## Smell: huge components

500-line SFCs mix concerns and defeat testing. Extract child components AND
composables (`useLessonProgress`) so logic tests run without mounting.

## Smell: excessive watchers

```ts
// BAD: reimplementing computed with side effects
watch(a, () => { total.value = a.value + b.value })
watch(b, () => { total.value = a.value + b.value })

// GOOD
const total = computed(() => a.value + b.value)
```

Watchers are for side effects (persist, focus, imperative APIs). If the output
is data, reach for computed first.

## Smell: duplicated reactive logic

Copy-pasted ref+computed+watch triplets across files → extract a composable
(`useLocalStorage(key)`) returning typed refs. Composition API's superpower is
*reusable behavior*, not just syntax sugar.
